carousels.name: It's all the same: what you're really looking for isn't p*rn

slides.title: Every p*rn video is the same video. [[What you're chasing was never in it.]]
slides.sub: The realization that makes p*rn urges lose their grip.

slides.title: It's [[all the same]]
slides.body: New tab. New video. New "type." Paid content, custom content, more extreme content. Many guys who quit say the same thing: none of it ever actually satisfied them.

slides.title: Your "type" is a [[clue]]
slides.body: Look at what you keep searching for in p*rn. It often mirrors a feeling you're avoiding — rejection, loneliness, feeling not good enough. The search isn't random. It's pointing at a wound.

slides.title: What you [[actually]] want
slides.body: To feel wanted. To feel close to someone. To hear you're good enough as you are. P*rn imitates those feelings for ten minutes — then leaves you emptier.

slides.title: When the urge hits, [[ask]]
items: What am I feeling right now — bored, lonely, rejected, stressed?
What do I actually need? A person? Rest? Reassurance?
Can p*rn give me that? (It never has.)
What's one real step toward it tonight?
slides.note: Did this hit? Send it to someone who keeps chasing the next video ↗

slides.title:
What you're missing
[[isn't p*rn.]]
slides.lead: Journal what's underneath the urge, talk it through with an AI coach and connect with people who get it.

slides.title: "I can stop p*rn whenever I want." [[It's Day 17. Prove it.]]
slides.sub: The excuse every addicted guy uses — and how to test it.

slides.title: Then why [[haven't]] you?
slides.body: If you could stop whenever, you'd have stopped the first time it cost you sleep, focus or a relationship. "Whenever" never comes.

slides.title: The [[test]]
slides.body: 30 days. No p*rn. No "almost p*rn." No loopholes. If it's easy, great — you were right. If it isn't, you've learned something important.

slides.title: Failing isn't [[shameful]]
slides.body: Failing the test doesn't make you weak. It means p*rn has more control than you thought. That's when the real work starts.

slides.title: Take the [[test]] properly
items: Block p*rn — don't rely on "I can stop."
Tell one person so you can't fake it.

carousels.name: The 24 hours after you say no to a p*rn urge

slides.title: What happens in the 24 hours [[after you say no to p*rn.]]
slides.sub: One "no" changes more than one night.

slides.title: The [[push]]
slides.body: The p*rn urge peaks. Your brain bargains. You leave the room anyway. That's the hardest minute of the day.

slides.title: The [[fade]]
slides.body: The urge drops. You realize it passed without p*rn. Your brain just learned it can survive the wave.

slides.title: The [[clean]] start
slides.body: No guilt. No hiding your phone. No "why did I do that." Many guys say this feeling is what keeps them going.

slides.title: The [[proof]]
slides.body:
One full day you chose something other than p*rn.

Stack those days and they become a different life.

slides.title: Can't fall asleep without p*rn? [[A 2025 study found a link.]]
slides.sub: Insomnia and p*rn addiction often travel together.

slides.title: Screened [[positive]]
slides.body: In a study of 1,008 young adults (Rhode Island, 2024 data, published 2025), 7.9% screened positive for p*rn addiction — about 1 in 13.

slides.title: The sleep [[link]]
slides.body: Insomnia was linked to higher odds of p*rn addiction, mainly in heterosexual men. It's a link, not proof of cause — but the loop is familiar to many.

slides.title: P*rn as a [[sleeping pill]]
slides.body: Many guys use p*rn to switch off at night. It "works" — until you can't sleep without it. That's dependence, not relaxation.

slides.title: Fall asleep [[without]] it
items: Read or breathe slowly instead of scrolling.
Expect a few rough nights — then it gets easier.

carousels.name: How often is too often? 5 honest tests

slides.title: How often is too often with p*rn? [[Forget the number. Take these 5 tests.]]
slides.sub: The answers that got the most upvotes on Reddit.

slides.title: Tests [[1–2]]
items: Do you choose p*rn over a willing partner? If yes, it's a problem.
Can you stay aroused with a real person? Many men say this was their first warning sign.

slides.title: Tests [[3–4]]
items: Have you watched p*rn somewhere you shouldn't — at work, in class, in the car?
Do you watch multiple times a day and can't stop when you try?

slides.title: Test [[5]]
items: Is it interfering with your life — sleep, work, relationships, confidence? That's the line most people draw.

slides.title: Failed [[one]]?
slides.body: Then it's not about the number anymore. P*rn is costing you something. Take that seriously.
